comments.body: These photos are from my brother and he insists that they’re not supposed to have pigeons there. Is he wrong or can someone give more context? He says he never sees pigeons.

The shape of the head is very distinctive for *Columba* species. The only Columba species in the Americas is *C. livia* var *domestica* (feral/domestic rock pigeon).
Also the likelihood of a wild bird having a similar "salt-and-pepper" color pattern is very low (not impossible, but significantly more likely to occur in feral/domestic rock pigeons on account of their domestic ancestry).
Also there are very much pigeons in the area: https://ebird.org/map/rocpig?env.minX=-179.99999999291&env.minY=-55.75832834475&env.maxX=179.99999999291&env.maxY=71.9081724700314
Even if there's not "supposed to be" pigeons in this specific neighborhood, there are pigeons in the vicinity and pigeons are known for moving around a lot.
